findings.evidence: `rg` shows lines 101, 107, 114, and 146 use only `@[reassoc]`; Mathlib marks the underlying forms as simp-normalization lemmas: `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Mon.lean:216 attribute [to_additive existing (attr := reassoc (attr := simp))] IsMonHom.one_hom IsMonHom.mul_hom`, `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Grp.lean:323 @[to_additive (attr := reassoc (attr := simp))] theorem inv_hom`, and `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Comma/Over/Basic.lean:72 @[reassoc (attr := simp)] theorem w`.
findings.fix: Tag these wrappers as `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]` unless a specific lemma would loop; these equations orient from a composed structure map to its normal form.
findings.issue: `Hom.one_hom`, `Hom.mul_hom`, `Hom.inv_hom`, and `Hom.toSchemeHom_comp_hom` are characteristic public API lemmas but are only tagged `@[reassoc]`, so the abelian-variety names do not participate in simp normalization.

summary: The public homomorphism surface is mostly narrow, but its characteristic preservation/base-compatibility lemmas are exposed without the normal-form simp annotations users need downstream.
